proof_interface_review: 1.1: The union of every G_beta stays inside one fixed polished-tail class with theta_1=0, so the conservative supplier gives one L and uniform epsilon_n; increasing L to at least 1 preserves this.

1.2: The displayed T_n expectation is finite under every ell2 truth since kappa is bounded and sum i^(-2-2p) converges. The same observable sum controls the means for all a>=0; trace is finite for all a>0. This correctly avoids substituting a random selector into separate fixed-a almost-sure events.

1.3 and 2.1: With e_i=i^(2beta)theta_i^2, the low-region multiplier is at most N^(-min(1,2d)). The high-region exponent gives N^(-2d); monotonicity is uniform once log N is large. The fixed D gives the strict score-threshold bound throughout [0,beta-D/log n]. The arbitrary-truth lower bracket is the correct interface, and beta_->0 makes selector zero uniformly negligible.

2.2: Every positive-selector posterior gives H={u_1=0} mass zero since its first variance is (1+n kappa_1^2)^(-1)>0. Removing H therefore preserves credibility. The zero branch is exactly the whole space and makes no ell2-posterior assertion.

3.1: Splitting variance at N bounds trace by one K n^(-2a/q_a) uniformly for a>=beta_-/2. Markov, monotone coupling and the bounded derivative of a/q_a absorb D/log n into a constant and prove the no-log diameter rate with vanishing bad-event probability.

3.2: Coordinate partial sums, Borel selector and parameter integration give a Borel graph and quantile. Finite trace and nondegenerate first coordinate make the quantile finite and positive. Deleting H leaves the ball dense and hence retains its diameter. Zero branch has measurable infinite diameter.

4.1: Subtracting P(E)=1-gamma gives exactly P(Z intersect E^c)-P(Z^c intersect E intersect {theta outside B}); delta_n+epsilon_n controls both terms. Independence is unnecessary. All original constants, compact beta range, norm lower bound and unrestricted set geometry remain intact.

proof_interface_review: 1.1: The actual PL embedding definition supplies a subcomplex image in some finite linear triangulation T0. This is a supplied defining clause, not a claim that arbitrary TOP embeddings are tame.

2.1: T and T0 are linear triangulations of the same embedded polyhedron Q. Intersections and their faces form a finite convex cell complex by the exact intersection supplier; its compatible triangulation refines each original simplex. This directly handles the two given triangulations and does not misuse the narrower common-refinement lemma as if they were already subdivisions of a fixed third complex.

The image subcomplex in T0 is a union of T0 simplices; each is a union of refined cells and simplices. All refined simplices contained in f(P) cover it, and all their faces remain contained in f(P), giving a subcomplex. Empty P/Q when admissible and dimension-zero/one-point images work; no positive dimension is needed.
